The condition can be satisfied exactly when the space of bivariate polynomials of total degree ≤ k has at least as many coefficients as the number of ordered vertex pairs \((i,j)\) with \(i\neq j\).  
There are \(n(n-1)\) such ordered pairs, while the number of monomials of total degree ≤ k is  

\[
\binom{k+2}{2}= \frac{(k+2)(k+1)}{2}.
\]

Hence we need  

\[
\frac{(k+2)(k+1)}{2}\;\ge\;n(n-1).
\]

Solving the quadratic inequality for \(k\) gives  

\[
k \ge \frac{-3+\sqrt{\,1+8n(n-1)\,}}{2}.
\]

Since \(k\) must be an integer, the smallest admissible degree is  

\[
\boxed{k=\Big\lceil\frac{-3+\sqrt{\,1+8n(n-1)\,}}{2}\Big\rceil}.
\]

This bound is tight: for any \(k\) smaller than this value the number of monomials is insufficient to prescribe the required values at all \(n(n-1)\) distinct points \((z_i,z_j)\), and thus no polynomial can realize the edge‑indicator condition for every tree on \(n\) vertices.  

**ANSWER:** \(k=\displaystyle\Big\lceil\frac{-3+\sqrt{\,1+8n(n-1)\,}}{2}\Big\rceil\).
